behavior_constraints: POST /api/v1/auth/login is limited to 5 requests per 60 seconds per source IP; the 6th request within the window returns HTTP 429 with body {"error":"rate limit exceeded"}
POST /api/v1/auth/register is limited to 3 requests per 60 seconds per source IP; the 4th request within the window returns HTTP 429 with body {"error":"rate limit exceeded"}
Login and register rate-limit counters are tracked independently and do not share a bucket
Non-auth endpoints are not affected by the auth rate limiter
Only Go standard library packages are used for the rate limiter implementation
Within the configured rate limits, login (success and credential failure) and registration continue to behave exactly as before
entities.summary: This round adds independent per-IP rate limiting to the auth login (5/60s) and register (3/60s) endpoints, returning HTTP 429 with {"error":"rate limit exceeded"} when exceeded, without affecting other endpoints.

instruction_head:
## Security Review: No Rate Limiting on Authentication Endpoints

The `/api/v1/auth/login` and `/api/v1/auth/register` endpoints accept an unlimited number of requests from any single IP address. An attacker can perform brute-force credential stuffing attacks at an unlimited rate, or abuse registration to flood the user database.

### Required Fix

Enforce per-IP rate limits on authentication endpoints:
